subject: maths
title: Pictograms, Tally Charts and Block Diagrams
seo_title: Year 2 Pictograms and Tally Charts Worksheets: Block Diagrams and Tables (Free, with Answers)
standard_text: Interpret and construct simple pictograms, tally charts, block diagrams and simple tables; ask and answer simple questions by counting the number of objects in each category and sorting the categories by quantity; ask and answer questions about totalling and comparing categorical data.
meta_desc: Free Year 2 maths worksheets on statistics: tally charts in groups of five, pictograms where one symbol stands for 1, 2, 5 or 10, block diagrams, simple tables, putting groups in order, and “how many more?” and “how many altogether?” questions. 100 questions with an answer key, following the National Curriculum.
key_big: Count carefully, and look at the key first.
key_sub: In a tally, the fifth mark goes across, so each group is 5. If 1 symbol = 2, half a symbol = 1. Altogether means add; how many more or how many fewer means subtract.
body_html:
What is data?

Data is information we collect. We can count votes, pets or minibeasts. Then we show the numbers in a tally chart, a pictogram, a block diagram or a table.

Tally charts

Make one mark for each thing you count. The fifth mark goes across the other four. This makes a group of 5. Count the groups in 5s, then count on the single marks.

Example

How many children have a cat?

1 group of 5 and 2 more: 5, then 6, 7.

Answer: 7 children

Pictograms

A pictogram uses pictures. Always look at the key first. If 1 symbol = 1, just count the symbols. If 1 symbol = 2, 5 or 10, count in 2s, 5s or 10s.

Example

Each star = 10 children. The Walk row has 4 stars. How many children walk?

Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40.

Answer: 40 children

Block diagrams

In a block diagram, each block stands for 1. The blocks sit in columns. Count the blocks, or read the number on the scale at the top of the column.

Tables and putting in order

In a table, find the right row, then read across. To put things in order, find the biggest number first, then the next biggest, and so on.

FruitNumber sold
Apples14
Bananas9
Pears6
Example

Put the fruit in order from most to fewest.

14 is the biggest, then 9, then 6.

Answer: apples, bananas, pears

Add or subtract?

The question saysDo this
altogether, in total, both, A or BAdd
how many more, how many fewer, differenceSubtract
Example

Dog 12, cat 7. How many more children have a dog than a cat?

12 − 7 = 5.

Answer: 5 more children

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting a tally group of 5 as 4 (forgetting the line across)The line across is the fifth mark
Drawing five lines and then a line across (a group of 6)Draw four lines, then the fifth goes across
Counting symbols and forgetting the keyIf 1 symbol = 5, count 5, 10, 15 …
Saying half a symbol is 2 when 1 symbol = 2Half of 2 is 1
Reading the wrong row or columnPut your finger on the label, then go across or up
Adding when the question says how many moreHow many more means subtract

faq.q: What statistics do children learn in Year 2?
faq.a: In Year 2 children read and make tally charts, pictograms, block diagrams and simple tables. They answer questions about totals and compare groups, such as “How many more?”.

faq.q: How do you teach tally charts in Year 2?
faq.a: Make one mark for each thing, and draw the fifth mark across the other four. Children then count the groups in 5s and count on the single marks.

faq.q: What is a block diagram in Year 2?
faq.a: A block diagram is like a bar chart made of blocks. Each block stands for 1 thing, so children can count the blocks or read the scale.

faq.q: What does the key on a pictogram mean?
faq.a: The key tells you what one symbol stands for, such as 1, 2, 5 or 10. If one symbol stands for 2, half a symbol stands for 1.

items.q: What number does this tally show?
items.e: Four lines with one line across make a group of 5. 1 group of 5. Count in 5s: 5. So it is 5.

items.q: What number does this tally show?
items.e: Four lines with one line across make a group of 5. 1 group of 5 and 2 more. Count in 5s: 5, then 6, 7. So it is 7.

items.q: What number does this tally show?
items.e: Four lines with one line across make a group of 5. 2 groups of 5. Count in 5s: 5, 10. So it is 10.

items.q: What number does this tally show?
items.e: Four lines with one line across make a group of 5. 2 groups of 5 and 3 more. Count in 5s: 5, 10, then 11, 12, 13. So it is 13.

items.q: What number does this tally show?
items.e: Four lines with one line across make a group of 5. 3 groups of 5 and 3 more. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, then 16, 17, 18. So it is 18.

items.q: How many children chose strawberry?
items.e: Find the Strawberry row. It has 3 groups of 5 and 1 more. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, then 16. So it is 16.

items.q: How many children chose oranges?
items.e: Find the Orange row. It has 2 groups of 5 and 3 more. Count in 5s: 5, 10, then 11, 12, 13. So it is 13.

items.q: How many worms were found?
items.e: Find the Worm row. It has 1 group of 5 and 1 more. Count in 5s: 5, then 6. So it is 6.

items.q: How many children chose yellow?
items.e: Find the Yellow row. It has 2 groups of 5 and 2 more. Count in 5s: 5, 10, then 11, 12. So it is 12.

items.q: Which row shows 14 children?
items.e: 14 is 5 + 5 + 4. The Tag row has 2 groups of 5 and 4 more. Count in 5s: 5, 10, then 11, 12, 13, 14. So it is 14.

items.q: Which row shows 9 children?
items.e: 9 is 5 + 4. The Hamster row has 1 group of 5 and 4 more. Count in 5s: 5, then 6, 7, 8, 9. So it is 9.

items.q: Which fruit is the most popular?
items.e: Count every row: Apple 7, Banana 5, Orange 13, Grapes 17. The biggest number is 17, for Grapes.

items.q: Which colour is the least popular?
items.e: Count every row: Yellow 12, Blue 7, Purple 18, Green 5. The smallest number is 5, for Green.

items.q: Which tally shows 8?
items.e: C is right: 1 group of 5 and 3 more. Count in 5s: 5, then 6, 7, 8. So it is 8. A: it has one mark too many; B: the groups have five upright lines and a line across, so each group is 6; D: it has one mark too few.

items.q: Which tally shows 13?
items.e: A is right: 2 groups of 5 and 3 more. Count in 5s: 5, 10, then 11, 12, 13. So it is 13. B: the groups have no line across, so they are hard to count in 5s; C: it has one mark too few; D: the groups have five upright lines and a line across, so each group is 6.

items.q: Which tally shows 17?
items.e: D is right: 3 groups of 5 and 2 more. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, then 16, 17. So it is 17. A: the groups have five upright lines and a line across, so each group is 6; B: it has one mark too many; C: the groups have no line across, so they are hard to count in 5s.

items.q: How many more children chose chocolate than mint?
items.e: Chocolate: 19. Mint: 5. How many more means find the difference: 19 − 5 = 14.

items.q: How many fewer worms than woodlice were found?
items.e: Woodlouse: 17. Worm: 6. How many fewer means find the difference: 17 − 6 = 11.

items.q: How many children voted altogether?
items.e: Count every row: Hopscotch 2, Football 13, Skipping 7, Tag 14. Then add: 2 + 13 + 7 + 14 = 36.

items.q: How many children are shown altogether?
items.e: Count every row: Rabbit 10, Fish 19, Cat 14, Hamster 9. Then add: 10 + 19 + 14 + 9 = 52.

items.q: How many pigeons were seen?
items.e: Each circle = 1 bird. Count the circles in the Pigeon row: 2 pigeons.
Each star = 1 car. Count the stars in the White row: 4 cars.

items.q: How many children come by scooter?
items.e: Each square = 1 child. Count the squares in the Scooter row: 6 children.
Each heart = 1 child. Count the hearts in the Cat row: 6 children.

items.q: How many children chose grapes?
items.e: Each circle = 1 child. Count the circles in the Grapes row: 4 children.
Each star = 1 child. Count the stars in the Scooter row: 5 children.

items.q: Which row shows 3 children?
items.e: Each square = 1 child. Look for the row with 3 squares. That is Green.
Each heart = 1 child. Look for the row with 6 hearts. That is Strawberry.

items.q: Which game is the most popular?
items.e: Each circle = 1 child. The Football row has the most circles: 9.
Each star = 1 bird. The Blackbird row has the most stars: 8.

items.q: Which minibeast did they find the fewest of?
items.e: Each square = 1 minibeast. The Spider row has the fewest squares: 3.
Each heart = 1 car. The Silver row has the fewest hearts: 1.

items.q: How many more children come by scooter than walk to school?
items.e: Each circle = 1 child. Scooter: 4. Walk: 1. How many more means find the difference: 4 − 1 = 3.
Each star = 1 child. Skipping: 6. Football: 2. How many fewer means find the difference: 6 − 2 = 4.

items.q: How many more red cars than silver cars went past?
items.e: Each square = 1 car. Red: 9. Silver: 3. How many more means find the difference: 9 − 3 = 6.
Each heart = 1 child. Pear: 5. Grapes: 4. Add them: 5 + 4 = 9.

items.q: How many spiders and ladybirds were found altogether?
items.e: Each circle = 1 minibeast. Spider: 9. Ladybird: 8. Add them: 9 + 8 = 17.
Each star = 1 bird. Blue tit: 3. Blackbird: 9. Add them: 3 + 9 = 12.

items.q: How many children are shown altogether?
items.e: Each square = 1 child. Count every row: Cat 6, Fish 3, Dog 2, Hamster 8. Add them: 6 + 3 + 2 + 8 = 19.
Each heart = 1 child. Count every row: Strawberry 8, Mint 2, Chocolate 7, Vanilla 5. Add them: 8 + 2 + 7 + 5 = 22.

items.q: How many children chose yellow?
items.e: Look at the key: each circle = 2 children, so half a circle = 1. The Yellow row has 3 circles. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6. So it is 6 children.
Look at the key: each star = 5 children. The Apple row has 3 stars. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15. So it is 15 children.

items.q: How many children walk to school?
items.e: Look at the key: each square = 10 children. The Walk row has 9 squares. Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90. So it is 90 children.

items.q: How many ladybirds were found?
items.e: Look at the key: each circle = 2 minibeasts, so half a circle = 1. The Ladybird row has 7 circles. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14. So it is 14 ladybirds.
Look at the key: each star = 2 children, so half a star = 1. The Fish row has 2 stars and half a star. Count in 2s: 2, 4, then 1 more for the half. So it is 5 children.
Look at the key: each star = 5 children. The Vanilla row has 3 stars. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15. So it is 15 children.

items.q: How many children chose purple?
items.e: Look at the key: each square = 10 children. The Purple row has 7 squares. Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70. So it is 70 children.
Look at the key: each star = 2 cars, so half a star = 1. The Red row has 2 stars and half a star. Count in 2s: 2, 4, then 1 more for the half. So it is 5 cars.

items.q: Each square stands for 5 children. 20 children chose tag. How many squares go in the Tag row?
items.e: Count in 5s until you reach 20: 5, 10, 15, 20. That is 4 steps, so draw 4 squares, not 20.

items.q: Each circle stands for 10 children. 60 children walk to school. How many circles go in the Walk row?
items.e: Count in 10s until you reach 60: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60. That is 6 steps, so draw 6 circles, not 60.

items.q: How many children chose football?
items.e: Look at the key: each square = 10 children. The Football row has 6 squares. Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60. So it is 60 children.

items.q: How many pigeons were seen?
items.e: Look at the key: each square = 2 birds, so half a square = 1. The Pigeon row has 3 squares and half a square. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, then 1 more for the half. So it is 7 pigeons.

items.q: Which colour is the most popular?
items.e: Look at the key: each circle = 5 children. The Blue row has the most circles: 6 circles. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30. So it is 30 children.

items.q: Each star stands for 2 children. 7 children chose mint. What goes in the Mint row?
items.e: Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6. That is 3 stars, which makes 6. 1 more is half of 2, so add half a star. Draw 3 and a half stars.

items.q: Which way do the fewest children come to school?
items.e: Look at the key: each square = 10 children. The Bike row has the fewest squares: 3 squares. Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30. So it is 30 children.
Look at the key: each heart = 5 children. Grapes: 3 hearts = 15. Banana: 1 heart = 5. How many more means subtract: 15 − 5 = 10.

items.q: How many more children chose skipping than football?
items.e: Look at the key: each circle = 10 children. Skipping: 4 circles = 40. Football: 2 circles = 20. How many more means subtract: 40 − 20 = 20.

items.q: How many children have a hamster or a rabbit?
items.e: Look at the key: each square = 2 children, so half a square = 1. Hamster: 15. Rabbit: 6. Altogether means add: 15 + 6 = 21.

items.q: How many children chose vanilla or chocolate?
items.e: Look at the key: each square = 10 children. Vanilla: 20. Chocolate: 60. Altogether means add: 20 + 60 = 80.
Look at the key: each heart = 5 children. Football: 7 hearts = 35. Hopscotch: 4 hearts = 20. How many fewer means subtract: 35 − 20 = 15.

sets.title: Block diagrams, tables and putting in order

items.q: How many blue tits were seen?
items.e: Each block = 1 bird. Count the blocks in the Blue tit column: 2. The top of the column is at 2 on the scale.

items.q: How many children chose skipping?
items.e: Each block = 1 child. Count the blocks in the Skipping column: 10. The top of the column is at 10 on the scale.

items.q: How many children come by car?
items.e: Each block = 1 child. Count the blocks in the Car column: 12. The top of the column is at 12 on the scale.

items.q: Which column shows 6 children?
items.e: Each block = 1 child. The Dog column has 6 blocks.

items.q: Which colour of car went past the most?
items.e: Each block = 1 car. The tallest column is White: 12.

items.q: Which weather did March have on the fewest days?
items.e: Each block = 1 day. The shortest column is Sunny: 3.

items.q: How many more children chose green than purple?
items.e: Each block = 1 child. Green: 11. Purple: 2. How many more means find the difference: 11 − 2 = 9.

items.q: How many fewer children chose pears than oranges?
items.e: Each block = 1 child. Orange: 11. Pear: 2. How many fewer means find the difference: 11 − 2 = 9.

items.q: Put the flavours in order from most to fewest.
items.e: Read each one: Strawberry 9, Mint 6, Vanilla 12, Chocolate 8. Biggest first: Vanilla (12), Strawberry (9), Chocolate (8), Mint (6).

items.q: Put the minibeasts in order from fewest to most.
items.e: Read each one: Woodlouse 3, Spider 8, Snail 2, Worm 7. Smallest first: Snail (2), Woodlouse (3), Worm (7), Spider (8).

items.q: How many white cars went past?
items.e: Find the White row, then read the number next to it: 14 cars.

items.q: How many children chose purple?
items.e: Find the Purple row, then read the number next to it: 16 children.

items.q: Which pet do the most children have?
items.e: Read the table. The biggest number is Cat: 17.

items.q: Put the fruits in order from most to fewest.
items.e: Read each one: Orange 6, Grapes 14, Pear 12, Banana 13. Biggest first: Grapes (14), Banana (13), Pear (12), Orange (6).

items.q: How many minibeasts were found altogether?
items.e: Read the table. Add all the numbers: 16 + 2 + 3 + 6 = 27.

items.q: How many more robins than blue tits were seen?
items.e: Read the table. Robin: 16. Blue tit: 13. How many more means find the difference: 16 − 13 = 3.

items.q: How many children from Class 2B go to Choir?
items.e: Find the Choir row, then go across to the Class 2B column: 13. (6 is the Class 2A column.)

items.q: How many children go to Football altogether?
items.e: Football row: Class 2A 9, Class 2B 12. Altogether means add: 9 + 12 = 21.

items.q: Which way do the fewest children come to school?
items.e: Read the table. The smallest number is Car: 2.

items.q: Put the flavours in order from fewest to most.
items.e: Read each one: Chocolate 14, Strawberry 18, Vanilla 6, Mint 8. Smallest first: Vanilla (6), Mint (8), Chocolate (14), Strawberry (18).

items.q: How many more sunny days than rainy days were there in March?
items.e: Sunny: 12 blocks. Rainy: 8 blocks. How many more means subtract: 12 − 8 = 4.

items.q: How many days were rainy or windy?
items.e: Rainy: 8. Windy: 4. Or means put them together: 8 + 4 = 12.

items.q: March has 31 days. How many days were not sunny?
items.e: Sunny: 12. 31 − 12 = 19 days were not sunny. Check: 8 + 7 + 4 = 19.

items.q: Each child in Class 2 has one pet. How many children are in the tally chart?
items.e: Dog: 5 and 4 more = 9. Cat: 5 and 2 more = 7. Fish: 4. Rabbit: 5 and 1 more = 6. 9 + 7 + 4 + 6 = 26. (Counting each group of 5 as 4 gives 23.)

items.q: How many fewer children have a fish than a cat?
items.e: Cat: 7. Fish: 4. How many fewer means subtract: 7 − 4 = 3.

items.q: How many worms and snails were found altogether?
items.e: Each circle = 2, so half a circle = 1. Worms: 4 and a half circles = 9. Snails: 2 circles = 4. 9 + 4 = 13. (Counting the circles gives 7.)

items.q: How many more worms than spiders were found?
items.e: Worms: 9. Spiders: 1 and a half circles = 3. 9 − 3 = 6. (3 is the difference in circles, not minibeasts.)
Each star = 5. Apple 4 stars = 20, banana 3 stars = 15, grapes 6 stars = 30, orange 2 stars = 10. 20 + 15 + 30 + 10 = 75. (15 is the number of stars.)
Grapes: 6 stars = 30. Oranges: 2 stars = 10. 30 − 10 = 20. (4 is the difference in stars.)
Grapes got 30. Apple 20 + orange 10 = 30. Apple and banana make 35, banana and orange make 25.
Banana had 3 stars = 15. 15 + 5 = 20 votes. That is one more star. (8 comes from adding 5 to the 3 stars.)
Each heart = 10. Amelia has 6 hearts = 60. 60 + 40 = 100, so she needs 40 more. (94 comes from 100 − 6, counting the hearts.)
Oliver: 4 hearts = 40. Harry: 3 hearts = 30. 40 + 30 = 70. (7 is the number of hearts.)

items.q: How many pieces of fruit were sold altogether?
items.e: Add all the numbers: 14 + 9 + 6 + 11 = 40. (29 leaves out the satsumas.)

items.q: Put the fruit in order from most sold to fewest sold.
items.e: Apples 14, satsumas 11, bananas 9, pears 6. Biggest first: apples, satsumas, bananas, pears.

items.q: Class 2 counted birds in the garden. How many birds did they see altogether?
items.e: Robin 8, sparrow 13, blackbird 6, pigeon 11. 8 + 13 + 6 + 11 = 38. (Counting each group of 5 as 4 gives 33.)

items.q: How many fewer blackbirds than pigeons did they see?
items.e: Pigeons: 2 groups of 5 and 1 more = 11. Blackbirds: 5 and 1 more = 6. 11 − 6 = 5.

items.q: There are 28 children in Class 2. The rest came by scooter. How many children came by scooter?
items.e: Step 1: add the columns: 11 + 7 + 4 + 3 = 25. Step 2: 28 − 25 = 3 children came by scooter. (25 is the number shown, not the answer.)

items.q: Zara reads 4 more books. How many books has she read now?
items.e: Each square = 2, so half a square = 1. Zara: 1 and a half squares = 3. 3 + 4 = 7. (Counting half a square as 2 gives 8.)

items.q: How many more books did Kai read than Zara?
items.e: Kai: 4 squares = 8. Zara: 3. 8 − 3 = 5. (Adding gives 11.)
